Zeus.what: Infant Zeus is hidden in Crete by Rhea while Cronus swallows a stone.
Zeus frees his siblings, defeats the Titans and draws lots for rule of the sky.
Zeus swallows Metis and Athena springs armed from his head.
Zeus summons Hercules against the giants and buries Typhon under Etna after losing his sinews.
Zeus seduces Io and turns her into a cow.
Zeus takes Amphitryon's shape and fathers Hercules on Alcmena.

Poseidon.what: Poseidon receives the trident and rule of the sea.
Poseidon sends the bull and makes Pasiphae love it.
Poseidon contests Attica with Athena, loses, and floods the land.
Poseidon destroys Erechtheus and his house.

Hera.what: Hera hunts Latona until she bears Artemis and Apollo.
Hera sets Argus to guard Io after she becomes a cow.
Hera delays Alcmena's labour and drives Hercules mad.
Hera sends storms against Hercules and is hung from Olympus by Zeus.

Apollo.what: Apollo takes Delphi, kills Python and Tityus, and flays Marsyas.
Apollo fights Hercules at Delphi over the tripod until Zeus intervenes.
Apollo and Artemis kill Niobe's children.
Apollo trades with Hermes for the cattle and later serves Admetus.

Hercules.what: Hercules is born, strangles Hera's serpents, defeats the Minyans, and burns his children in madness.
Hercules performs the first eight labours for Eurystheus.
Hercules takes Hippolyte's belt, rescues Hesione and fetches Geryon's cattle.
Hercules fetches the apples, tricks Atlas and brings back Cerberus.
Hercules kills Iphitus, fights Apollo, is sold to Omphale and sacks Troy.
Hercules wages wars, is poisoned by Deianira's tunic and becomes immortal on Oeta.

Hermes.what: Hermes helps steal back Zeus's sinews from Typhon.
Hermes kills Argus and purifies the Danaids.
Hermes helps Perseus and gives him a sickle.
Newborn Hermes steals Apollo's cattle and invents the lyre.

Athena.what: Athena springs armed from Zeus's head.
Athena guides Perseus and receives the Gorgon's head.
Athena advises Cadmus to sow the dragon's teeth.
Athena wins Attica with the olive.

Ares.what: Ares is bound by the Aloads.
Ares kills Halirrhothius and is acquitted at the Areopagus.

Artemis.what: Artemis is born at Delos and kills Orion.
Artemis kills the Aloads by a trick.
Artemis sends the boar against Calydon.
Artemis shoots Callisto, who is turned into a bear.

Hephaestus.what: Hephaestus is thrown from heaven and lamed on Lemnos.
Hephaestus pursues Athena and Erichthonius is born from his seed.

Pluto.what: Pluto abducts Persephone and makes her stay a third of the year.
Pluto's realm is entered by Hercules, who takes Cerberus.

Aphrodite.what: Aphrodite gives Melanion the golden apples to win Atalanta.

Chiron.what: Chiron is wounded by Hercules and gives up his immortality.
Chiron saves Peleus and raises Achilles.

Demeter.what: Demeter searches for Persephone, nurses Demophon, and gives Triptolemus wheat.

Earth.what: Earth bears the Titans and urges them against Sky.
Earth bears the giants and Typhon against the gods.

Eurystheus.what: Eurystheus sets the labours and rejects some of them.
Eurystheus orders the belt of Hippolyte and Geryon's cattle.
Eurystheus orders the apples and receives Cerberus.
Eurystheus hounds the Heraclids and is killed by Hyllus at Athens.

Minos.what: Minos wins Crete, prays for Poseidon's bull and keeps it.
Minos searches for Glaucus and forces Polyidus to teach divination.
Minos mourns Androgeus and besieges Athens, demanding youths for the Minotaur.

Prometheus.what: Prometheus makes men, steals fire and is chained until Hercules frees him.
Prometheus is freed by Hercules, who shoots the eagle.

Theseus.what: Theseus lifts the rock and kills Periphetes and Sinis on the road to Athens.

Achelous.what: Achelous takes bull shape and is defeated by Hercules.

Dionysus.what: Dionysus is born from Semele's death and hidden.
Dionysus spreads his rites and punishes Lycurgus, Pentheus and pirates.

Creon.what: Creon forbids burial of the Argive dead.

Pollux.what: Pollux shares his immortality with the dead Castor.

Typhon.what: Typhon attacks heaven, maims Zeus and is buried under Etna.

Admetus.what: Apollo helps Admetus win Alcestis, who dies in his place.

Castor.what: Castor is killed by Idas in the cattle raid.

Cephalus.what: Cephalus's unfailing dog chases the vixen and both are turned to stone.
Cephalus accidentally kills his wife Procris.

Cepheus.what: Cepheus is king of Ethiopia, whose daughter Andromeda is rescued by Perseus.

Diomedes.what: Diomedes avenges Oeneus, kills Agrius's sons and buries Oeneus.
Diomedes is killed by Hercules, who takes his man-eating mares.

Europa.what: Zeus carries Europa to Crete as a bull.

Eurytion.what: Eurytion herds Geryon's cattle and is killed by Hercules.
Eurytion purifies Peleus and is accidentally killed by him.

Eurytus.what: Eurytus's daughter Iole is refused to Hercules, and Iphitus is murdered.

Persephone.what: Persephone is carried off to Hades, eats a pomegranate seed and must return yearly.

Lycus.what: Lycus usurps Thebes and is killed by Zethus and Amphion.

Lynceus.what: Lynceus is spared by Hypermnestra on the wedding night.
Lynceus dies in the fight over the cattle.

Nauplius.what: Nauplius buys Catreus's daughters to sell abroad.

Neleus.what: Neleus grows up with Pelias and founds Pylus.

Oeneus.what: Oeneus receives the vine, neglects Artemis and later is tormented and killed by Agrius's sons.

Peleus.what: Peleus is purified, escapes slander, marries Thetis and fathers Achilles.

Proetus.what: Proetus quarrels with Acrisius and gets Tiryns; his daughters go mad.
Proetus purifies Bellerophon and sends him off with a letter ordering his death.

Thetis.what: Thetis is won by Peleus, tests Achilles in fire and leaves.

Adrastus.what: Adrastus gives his daughters to Polynices and Tydeus and leads the seven against Thebes.
Adrastus appeals to Athens for burial of the dead.

Aegeus.what: Aegeus lies with Aethra and leaves a sword and sandals under a rock.

Agenor.what: Agenor's family scatters in search of Europa.

Agrius.what: Agrius's sons seize Calydon and torment Oeneus.

Alcmena.what: Alcmena bears Hercules after Zeus takes Amphitryon's shape.

Amphiaraus.what: Amphiaraus foresees doom, is forced to war by Eriphyle, and is swallowed by the earth.

Stheneboea.what: Stheneboea falsely accuses Bellerophon after he rejects her.

Antigone.what: Antigone buries Polynices and is entombed alive.

Minotaur.what: The Minotaur is born to Pasiphae and shut in the Labyrinth.
The Minotaur receives Athens' tribute of youths in the labyrinth.

Atalanta.what: Atalanta joins the Calydonian boar hunt and receives the skin.
Atalanta is exposed, raised by hunters, races suitors and marries Melanion.

Atlas.what: Atlas fetches the apples and is tricked back under the sky by Hercules.

Cadmus.what: Cadmus follows the cow, founds Thebes, kills the dragon and marries Harmonia.
Cadmus and Harmonia are turned into serpents and sent to Elysium.

Callirrhoe.what: Callirrhoe's sons grow up at once and avenge Alcmaeon.

Ceyx.what: Ceyx and his wife Alcyone are turned into birds for their pride.

Daedalus.what: Daedalus builds the wooden cow for Pasiphae and the Labyrinth for the Minotaur.

Dawn.what: Dawn, in love with Orion, carries him off to Delos.

Deucalion.what: Deucalion and Pyrrha survive Zeus's flood in a chest and make new people from stones.

Eteocles.what: Eteocles, son of Oedipus, is born into the cursed house of Thebes.
Eteocles agrees to alternate rule with Polynices, then banishes him and defends Thebes.
Eteocles and Polynices kill each other in the battle at Thebes.

Glaucus.what: Glaucus, Minos's child, drowns in a honey jar and is revived by Polyidus.
Glaucus is forced to learn divination, then forgets it when he spits into Polyidus's mouth.

Helen.what: Helen is born to Leda and Zeus and abducted by Theseus.

Hesione.what: Hesione is exposed to the sea monster and saved by Hercules.
Hercules takes Troy and gives Hesione to Telamon as a prize.

Hyacinth.what: Hyacinth is loved by Thamyris and Apollo, and killed by Apollo's quoit.

Idas.what: Idas carries off Marpessa and she chooses him over Apollo.
Idas cheats the Dioscuri over the cattle and kills Castor, then is struck by Zeus.

Iole.what: Hercules wins the archery contest but Eurytus refuses to give him Iole.
Hercules sacks Oechalia and takes Iole captive.

Iphicles.what: Iphicles is born as twin of Hercules to Alcmena and Amphitryon.

Jason.what: Jason is sent by Pelias for the Golden Fleece and has the Argo built.
Jason wins the fleece at Colchis with Medea's drugs and flees with her.
Jason abandons Medea in Corinth; she kills Glauce and her children.

Laomedon.what: Laomedon cheats Apollo and Poseidon and denies Hercules his reward for saving Hesione.
Hercules sails against Laomedon and takes Ilium.
Laomedon, son of Ilus, reigns at Troy and fathers Tithonus and Priam.

Latona.what: Hera hunts Latona until she bears Artemis and Apollo on Delos.
Tityus assaults Latona and is shot by her children.
Niobe boasts of having more children than Latona; Artemis and Apollo kill them.

Lycurgus.what: Lycurgus drives out Dionysus, is maddened, kills his son and is put to death.

Medusa.what: Perseus beheads Medusa with the help of Hermes and Athena.

Menelaus.what: Menelaus is chosen as Helen's husband from the suitors.

Nereus.what: Hercules binds the shape-shifting Nereus until he reveals the way.

Niobe.what: Niobe boasts of her children; they are killed and she turns to stone.

Orpheus.what: Orpheus goes to Hades for Eurydice, loses her, and is torn apart by Maenads.
Orpheus counters the Sirens' song on the Argo's voyage home.

Parthenopaeus.what: Parthenopaeus joins the seven leaders marching on Thebes and dies in the battle.
Atalanta's son Parthenopaeus goes to war against Thebes.

Periboea.what: Oeneus marries Periboea, with varying accounts of her origin.

Phineus.what: The Argonauts free Phineus from the Harpies and he advises them on the Clashing Rocks.
Perseus turns Phineus and his fellow conspirators to stone.

Priam.what: Podarces is ransomed by Hesione and renamed Priam.
Priam's infant Paris is exposed after Hecuba's dream; Paris later takes Helen.

Polynices.what: Polynices is born to Oedipus, son of the cursed house.
Polynices is banished, marries at Argos, and bribes Eriphyle with the necklace.
Polynices leads the seven against Thebes and kills Eteocles, dying with him.
Creon leaves Polynices unburied; Antigone is entombed alive for burying him.

Praxithea.what: Praxithea cries out at the sight of the child in the fire.

Telamon.what: Telamon is first to enter Troy and receives Hesione.
Telamon takes refuge at Salamis, inherits it and fathers Ajax and Teucer.

Tiresias.what: Tiresias's blindness and prophecy are explained; he speaks at the battle of Thebes.
Tiresias advises the Thebans to flee and dies at Tilphussa.

Tithonus.what: Dawn loves Tithonus, son of Laomedon.

Tydeus.what: Tydeus is exiled, marries Deipyle, fathers Diomedes and dies at Thebes.
Tydeus fights Polynices at Argos and marries Adrastus's daughter.
Tydeus's embassy to Thebes defeats the Thebans and kills the ambush.

Tyndareus.what: Tyndareus is expelled by Hippocoon and returns; Helen's suitors swear the oath to him.

Acastus.what: Acastus abandons Peleus on Pelion after Astydamia's slander.

Acrisius.what: Acrisius quarrels with twin Proetus and divides Argos from Tiryns.
Acrisius locks Danae away and casts her and Perseus into the sea.
Perseus's discus kills Acrisius at Larissa, fulfilling the oracle.

Aegimius.what: Hercules fights for Aegimius, king of the Dorians.

Aegina.what: Zeus carries off Aegina; her son Aeacus becomes a pious king.

Aethra.what: Aethra lies with Aegeus and conceives Theseus.
Aethra's son Theseus lifts the rock and sets out for Athens.

Agave.what: Agave tears her son Pentheus apart in Dionysus's frenzy.

Agelaus.what: Agelaus, a servant, raises the exposed infant Paris.

Alcestis.what: Alcestis dies in place of Admetus and is sent back up.

Alcmaeon.what: Alcmaeon leads the Epigoni and sacks Thebes.
Alcmaeon kills Eriphyle, is pursued by a Fury and is killed over the necklace.

Aleus.what: Aleus's daughter Auge bears Hercules' child; the land turns barren and she is condemned.

Iobates.what: Iobates sends Bellerophon against the Chimera.
Iobates shows Bellerophon the letter, gives him Philonoe and the kingdom.

Amphictyon.what: Amphictyon expels Cranaus and becomes king of Athens.

Amphidamas.what: Hercules bursts his bonds and kills Busiris and Amphidamas.

Amycus.what: Pollux kills Amycus in a boxing match.

Androgeus.what: Androgeus wins the Panathenian games and dies; Minos mourns.

Apis.what: Aetolus kills Apis and flees, naming Aetolia.
Apis, a tyrant, is slain by Thelxion and Telchis and later deified.

Arcas.what: Arcas, son of Callisto, is saved and goes to Maia.

Argus.what: Argus builds the Argo for Jason's voyage to Colchis.
Argus, the many-eyed guard of Io, is killed by Hermes.

Ascalaphus.what: Ascalaphus testifies that Persephone ate the pomegranate seed and is buried under a rock.

Asopus.what: Asopus pursues Zeus, who carried off Aegina, and is driven back by thunderbolts.

Asteria.what: Asteria becomes a quail and plunges into the sea, becoming the island Delos.

Athamas.what: Athamas, maddened, loses Ino's sons and settles elsewhere after the ram flight.

Auge.what: Hercules seduces Auge at Tegea; her son Telephus is exposed and she is sent abroad.
Auge bears Hercules' child in Athena's precinct and is condemned; Telephus becomes prince of Mysia.

Augeas.what: Augeas cheats Hercules of his reward after the stables are cleaned.
Hercules marches on Augeas and kills him, taking Elis.

Bellerophon.what: Bellerophon is falsely accused by Stheneboea, kills the Chimera on Pegasus and wins Lycia.

Bias.what: Melampus steals Phylacus' kine so Bias can win Pero.
Bias marries one of the cured Proetides alongside Melampus.

Capaneus.what: Capaneus joins the seven against Thebes and is struck down by a thunderbolt.

Cecrops.what: Cecrops founds Attica and judges the contest of Poseidon and Athena.

Celeus.what: Celeus, king of Eleusis, hosts Demeter, whose attempt to immortalize his child fails.

Cleopatra.what: Cleopatra hangs herself with Althaea after Meleager dies.

Cronus.what: Cronus mutilates Sky, becomes ruler, and swallows his children to avoid being overthrown.
Drugged by Metis, Cronus vomits up his children and is defeated by Zeus.

Curetes.what: The armed Curetes guard infant Zeus and drown out his cries.

Cycnus.what: Cycnus challenges Hercules until a thunderbolt parts the fighters.
Hercules kills Cycnus while fighting for Aegimius.

Danae.what: Acrisius locks Danae away; she bears Perseus and is cast into the sea in a chest.

Deianira.what: Hercules wins Deianira from Achelous; she smears the tunic with Nessus' blood and hangs herself.

Dryas.what: Dryas, son of Lycurgus, is killed by his maddened father.

Epaphus.what: Epaphus is born to Io in Egypt and becomes king.

Ephialtes.what: Ephialtes and Otus attack the gods and are killed by Artemis's trick.

Erechtheus.what: Erechtheus sacrifices a daughter and kills Eumolpus; Poseidon then destroys him and his house.

Erichthonius.what: Erichthonius is born from Hephaestus's seed and becomes king of Athens.

Eriphyle.what: Eriphyle is bribed with the necklace and forces Amphiaraus to join the war.
Alcmaeon kills his mother Eriphyle, bribed with the robe.

Eumolpus.what: Eumolpus fights for Eleusis against Athens and is killed by Erechtheus.

Eurydice.what: Orpheus goes to Hades for Eurydice and loses her by looking back.

Harmonia.what: Harmonia marries Cadmus at a wedding the gods attend.
Harmonia and Cadmus are turned into serpents and sent to Elysium.

Hebe.what: Hebe marries Hercules after he is raised to heaven.

Hecate.what: Hecate kills the giant Clytius with torches.

Hippocoon.what: Hippocoon expels Tyndareus and Icarius and is killed by Hercules.

Hyllus.what: Hyllus kills Eurystheus, then misreads the oracle and is defeated.

Hypermnestra.what: Hypermnestra alone spares her husband Lynceus on the wedding night.

Hypsipyle.what: Hypsipyle leaves infant Opheltes to show a spring, and a serpent kills him.

Icarius.what: Icarius receives wine from Dionysus and is killed by shepherds.

Ino.what: Ino plots against Phrixus and Helle, prompting Nephele to send the golden ram.
Hera maddens Ino and Athamas, and Ino becomes a sea goddess.

Iolaus.what: Iolaus helps Hercules defeat the Lernaean hydra.

Ismarus.what: Ismarus, son of Astacus, slays Hippomedon in the battle at Thebes.

Laodocus.what: Laodocus wins the javelin at the Nemean funeral games.

Learchus.what: Learchus is shot by his maddened father Athamas.
Learchus is killed by Athamas, driven mad by Hera.

Linus.what: Linus, Hercules' lyre teacher, is killed by Hercules, who is acquitted.

Maenalus.what: Maenalus, eldest son of Lycaon, urges the crime and is struck down by Zeus.

Maia.what: Maia raises Arcas in Arcadia after Callisto's death.
Maia bears Hermes, who steals Apollo's cattle and invents the lyre.

Megara.what: Megara is won by Hercules, who in madness burns their children.

Melampus.what: Melampus gains prophetic hearing, steals Phylacus' kine for Bias and cures Iphiclus.
Melampus cures the mad Proetides in exchange for shares of the kingdom.

Melanippus.what: Melanippus, son of Astacus, wounds Tydeus at Thebes.

Meleager.what: Meleager is fated to die by the brand, kills the boar and Thestius' sons.
Althaea burns the brand and Meleager dies.

Melicertes.what: Melicertes, son of Athamas and Ino, is lost in Athamas' madness.
Melicertes, son of Ino, becomes a sea deity.

Menoetes.what: Menoetes warns Geryon of Hercules' arrival at the cattle.
Menoetes, herdsman of Hades, wrestles Hercules and is subdued in the descent.

Metis.what: Metis gives Cronus the drug that makes him disgorge Zeus's siblings.
Zeus swallows Metis, and Athena springs from his head.

Nessus.what: Nessus ferries Deianira, is shot by Hercules, and gives her the false love charm.

Nestor.what: Nestor, youngest son of Neleus, is spared when Hercules destroys Pylus.

Oedipus.what: Oedipus, exposed as an infant, kills Laius on the road.
Oedipus solves the Sphinx's riddle, marries Jocasta, blinds himself and goes into exile.

Pasiphae.what: Pasiphae, made to love Poseidon's bull, bears the Minotaur with Daedalus' wooden cow.

Pegasus.what: Pegasus carries Bellerophon to kill the Chimera.

Phoenix.what: Phoenix goes to Troy with Achilles and Patroclus.

Phyleus.what: Phyleus testifies for Hercules against his father Augeas.
Hercules installs Phyleus as king of Elis.

Pirithous.what: Pirithous is bound in Hades for wooing Persephone.

Polyphontes.what: Polyphontes usurps Messene and is killed by Aepytus.

Rhea.what: Rhea hides the infant Zeus in Crete and gives Cronus a stone.
Rhea purifies and initiates the mad Dionysus in Phrygia.

Sky.what: Sky binds his children in Tartarus and is mutilated by Cronus.

Styx.what: Zeus honors Styx with the oath.

Sun.what: The Sun gives Hercules a golden goblet to cross the sea.

Talos.what: Talos guards Crete and is passed by the Argonauts.

Telegonus.what: Telegonus is killed by Hercules in wrestling at Torone.

Telephassa.what: Telephassa dies, after which Cadmus consults Delphi.

Telephus.what: Telephus, son of Hercules and Auge, is exposed and suckled by a doe.
Telephus is raised by herdsmen and becomes prince of Mysia.

Teuthras.what: Teuthras, prince of Mysia, marries Auge.

Thespius.what: Thespius lets Hercules father children on his fifty daughters.

Tisiphone.what: Tisiphone is born as a Fury from Sky's blood.

Tlepolemus.what: Tlepolemus kills Licymnius and goes to Rhodes.

Ulysses.what: Ulysses devises the oath for Helen's suitors.
Ulysses discovers Achilles at Lycomedes' court with a trumpet.

Abas.what: Abas is father of the twins Acrisius and Proetus.

Abderus.what: Abderus is devoured by the mares of Diomedes while Hercules is away

Acarnan.what: Acarnan grows up at once with his brother and helps avenge Alcmaeon

Achilles.what: Thetis tests infant Achilles in fire; Chiron raises him
Achilles is hidden at Lycomedes' court, discovered by Ulysses, and goes to Troy

Actaeon.what: Actaeon is turned into a deer and eaten by his dogs

Adonis.what: Adonis is born from the myrrh tree, shared by two goddesses, killed by a boar

Aeacus.what: Aeacus becomes a pious king of Aegina; his sons kill Phocus and are exiled

Aeetes.what: Aeetes sets Jason impossible tasks and loses the fleece and Medea

Aegipan.what: Aegipan helps Hermes steal back Zeus's sinews from Typhon

Egyptus.what: Egyptus quarrels with Danaus, whose daughters murder Egyptus's sons

Aeolus.what: Aeolus rules Thessaly and fathers many children

Aepytus.what: Aepytus avenges his father by killing Polyphontes

Aesculapius.what: Aesculapius becomes a healer who raises the dead
Zeus kills Aesculapius with a thunderbolt

Aetolus.what: Aetolus flees after killing Apis and names Aetolia

Alcyone.what: Alcyone and Ceyx are turned into birds for their pride

Alcyoneus.what: Alcyoneus attacks heaven and is killed by Hercules, dragged from his land

Paris.what: Paris is exposed as an infant, survives, takes Helen, and dies unhealed by Oenone

Otus.what: Otus and Ephialtes attack the gods and are killed by Artemis's trick

Althaea.what: Althaea hides the brand, then burns it, killing Meleager; she hangs herself

Althaemenes.what: Althaemenes flees to Rhodes and kicks his sister Apemosyne to death
Althaemenes unknowingly kills his father Catreus, then vanishes into a chasm

Amphion.what: Amphion and Zethus kill Lycus, bind Dirce to a bull, fortify Thebes

Amphitryon.what: Amphitryon accidentally kills Electryon and is exiled to Thebes
Amphitryon conquers the Taphian islands after Comaetho betrays her father

Amphoterus.what: Amphoterus grows up at once and helps avenge Alcmaeon

Amymone.what: Amymone finds the springs of Lerna with Poseidon's help

Ancaeus.what: Ancaeus is killed by the Calydonian boar

Anchius.what: Anchius is repelled by Hercules in the centaur fight

Andromeda.what: Andromeda is freed by Perseus from the sea monster

Antaeus.what: Antaeus is killed by Hercules, lifted from the earth

Antiope.what: Antiope's sons Zethus and Amphion take revenge on Lycus and Dirce

Apemosyne.what: Apemosyne is kicked to death by her brother Althaemenes on Rhodes after Hermes ravishes her.

Apsyrtus.what: Apsyrtus flees Colchis with Medea and Jason, then is murdered by Medea on the voyage home.

Opheltes.what: Infant Opheltes is left by Hypsipyle and killed by a serpent; the Nemean games honor him.

Arion.what: Arion carries Adrastus to safety, the only leader to escape from Thebes.

Aristomachus.what: Aristomachus is slain in battle after the Heraclids' first failed return.

Arsinoe.what: Arsinoe marries Alcmaeon after he kills Eriphyle; her father's sons later kill him.

Astydamia.what: Astydamia, refused by Peleus, slanders him to Acastus, who abandons Peleus on Pelion.

Boreas.what: Boreas seizes Orithyia and fathers the Boreads and two daughters.

Busiris.what: Busiris seizes Hercules for sacrifice in Egypt; Hercules bursts his bonds and kills him.

Calchas.what: Calchas declares Troy cannot fall without Achilles, prompting the search that finds him at Lycomedes' court.

Callisto.what: Callisto is seduced by Zeus, turned into a bear, shot by Artemis and made a constellation.

Catreus.what: Catreus, warned by an oracle, sails to Rhodes and is killed unknowingly by his son Althaemenes.

Cerberus.what: Cerberus is subdued by Hercules, shown to Eurystheus, and returned to Hades.

Chimera.what: The Chimera is killed by Bellerophon from Pegasus.

Circe.what: Circe purifies the Argonauts after Apsyrtus' murder, ending Zeus's storms.

Comaetho.what: Comaetho betrays her father Pterelaus to Amphitryon, enabling the conquest of the Taphian islands.

Cranaus.what: Cranaus reigns during Deucalion's flood and is expelled by Amphictyon.

Cresphontes.what: Cresphontes cheats in the lot-drawing with a clod of earth and wins Messene.
Cresphontes is killed, and his son Aepytus later avenges him.

Cteatus.what: Cteatus, a Molionide twin, is killed by Hercules in the war on Elis.

Cychreus.what: Cychreus gives Telamon refuge and leaves him Salamis.

Cyclopes.what: The Cyclopes, freed by Zeus, give him thunder and lightning and arm the gods.

Cyzicus.what: King Cyzicus is accidentally killed by the Argonauts.

Danaus.what: Danaus flees Egyptus to Argos and takes the kingdom.
Danaus marries his daughters to Egyptus's sons; all but Hypermnestra kill their husbands.

Dardanus.what: Dardanus leaves Samothrace and founds Dardania.

Deidamia.what: Deidamia, daughter of Lycomedes, is where Achilles is hidden before Troy.

Deiphobus.what: Deiphobus purifies Hercules after Neleus refuses.

Demophon.what: Demophon is nursed by Demeter in the fire and is consumed when Praxithea cries out.

Dictys.what: Dictys is made king of Seriphus by Perseus after Polydectes is petrified.

Dirce.what: Dirce is bound to a bull and killed by Zethus and Amphion.

Electryon.what: Electryon is accidentally killed by Amphitryon during the cattle raid.

Emathion.what: Emathion is killed by Hercules in Arabia.

Endymion.what: Endymion founds Elis and sleeps forever.

Jocasta.what: Jocasta marries Oedipus unknowingly and hangs herself when the truth emerges.

Erginus.what: Erginus demands tribute from Thebes and is defeated by Hercules.

Erigone.what: Erigone hangs herself after the dog Maera finds her father Icarius's body.

Eryx.what: Eryx wrestles Hercules over a bull and is killed.

Euripides.what: Euripides is cited for a version of Alcmaeon's children by Manto.

Evenus.what: Evenus drowns himself after Idas carries off his daughter Marpessa.

Gelanor.what: Gelanor yields the kingdom of Argos to Danaus.

Geryon.what: Geryon, three-bodied owner of red cattle, is killed by Hercules, who ships the cattle off.

Glauce.what: Glauce, Jason's new bride, is killed by Medea's poisoned robe.

Gration.what: Gration fights in the battle of the gods and giants and is slain.

Haemon.what: Haemon, son of Creon, is eaten by the Sphinx.

Halirrhothius.what: Halirrhothius assaults Alcippe and is killed by Ares, who is acquitted at the Areopagus.

Hecuba.what: Hecuba dreams of a firebrand, and the infant Paris is exposed.

Helle.what: Helle flees on the golden ram and falls into the sea and drowns.

Hellen.what: Hellen is born to Deucalion and Pyrrha, and his sons give their names to Greek peoples.

Hilaira.what: Hilaira is carried off with her sister by Castor and Pollux and marries Castor.

Hippolyte.what: Hippolyte, the Amazon queen, promises the belt but is killed by Hercules after Hera's trick.

Hippolytus.what: Hippolytus fights in the battle of the gods and giants and is slain by Hermes.

Hippomedon.what: Hippomedon, one of the seven against Thebes, takes a gate and is slain by Ismarus.

Melanion.what: Melanion wins the footrace against Atalanta with Aphrodite's golden apples and marries her.

Hippotes.what: Hippotes kills the soothsayer, bringing disaster on the Heraclids' expedition.

Hylaeus.what: Hylaeus, a centaur, is killed by Atalanta.

Hyleus.what: Hyleus is killed by the Calydonian boar.

Ialebion.what: Ialebion, son of Poseidon, tries to rob Hercules in Liguria and is killed.

Iambe.what: Iambe makes the disguised Demeter smile with her jokes at Eleusis.

Iasus.what: Iasus exposes his infant daughter Atalanta.

Idaea.what: Idaea, Phineus's second wife, slanders his sons.

Ilus.what: Ilus wins games in Phrygia, follows a cow and founds Ilium.

Io.what: Zeus seduces Io and turns her into a cow; she wanders to Egypt and bears Epaphus.

Iphianassa.what: Iphianassa goes mad with her sisters and is cured by Melampus.

Iphinoe.what: Iphinoe, eldest of Proetus's daughters, goes mad and dies during the pursuit.

Iphitus.what: Iphitus supports Hercules in the contest, then is thrown from the walls of Tiryns.

Itys.what: Itys is killed by his mother Procne and served to Tereus.

Laius.what: Laius ignores the oracle, exposes his infant son, and is killed by him at the crossroads.

Lycaon.what: Lycaon's fifty sons serve Zeus a slaughtered child; Zeus blasts them with thunderbolts.

Lycomedes.what: Lycomedes hides Achilles at his court until Ulysses discovers him.

Lysippe.what: Lysippe goes mad with her sisters and is cured by Melampus, who marries them.

Maera.what: Maera the dog finds Icarius's body, leading Erigone to hang herself.

Marpessa.what: Marpessa is carried off by Idas and chooses him over Apollo.

Marsyas.what: Marsyas challenges Apollo to a music contest, loses, and is flayed on a pine.

Medea.what: Medea's drugs help Jason win the fleece; she kills Apsyrtus on the flight.
Medea has Pelias boiled, then kills Glauce and her own children and flees.

Menoeceus.what: Menoeceus sacrifices himself during the battle at Thebes.

Metanira.what: Metanira's child Demophon is nursed by Demeter in the fire.

Nephele.what: Nephele sends Phrixus and Helle away on the golden ram to escape Ino's plot.

Nyctimus.what: Nyctimus is spared when Zeus blasts his brothers, and inherits the kingdom.

Oenone.what: Oenone refuses to heal the wounded Paris, who dies.

Omphale.what: Omphale buys Hercules, who performs deeds in her service.

Orion.what: Orion is blinded by Oenopion, healed by the sun, then killed by Artemis.

Orithyia.what: Orithyia is seized by Boreas and bears the Boreads and two daughters.

Orthus.what: Geryon's two-headed hound guards the cattle and is killed by Hercules.

Oxylus.what: Oxylus guides the Heraclids on a one-eyed horse to victory.

Pan.what: Pan teaches Apollo prophecy before Apollo kills Python.

Pandrosus.what: Pandrosus and her sisters open the chest and die.

Patroclus.what: Patroclus accompanies Achilles to Troy with Phoenix.

Pelias.what: Pelias sends Jason for the Golden Fleece after the one-sandal warning.
Pelias is boiled by his own daughters through Medea's trick.

Pentheus.what: Pentheus is torn apart by his mother Agave for opposing Dionysus.

Periphetes.what: Periphetes the Clubman is slain by Theseus, who takes his iron club.

Perseus.what: Perseus is born to Danae and cast into the sea in a chest.
Perseus beheads Medusa with help from Hermes and Athena.
Perseus slays the sea monster and frees Andromeda.
Perseus petrifies Polydectes and makes Dictys king of Seriphus.
Perseus kills Acrisius with a discus, fulfilling the oracle.

Phegeus.what: Phegeus purifies Alcmaeon, then his sons kill Alcmaeon over the necklace.
Alcmaeon's sons kill Phegeus' family and dedicate the necklace at Delphi.

Philomela.what: Philomela is raped and mutilated by Tereus, then helps kill Itys.

Philonoe.what: Philonoe is given in marriage to Bellerophon by Iobates.

Phocus.what: Phocus is killed by his half-brothers, who are exiled.

Pholus.what: Pholus hosts Hercules; opening the wine starts a centaur fight and Pholus dies.

Phrixus.what: Phrixus flies on the golden ram to Colchis.

Pittheus.what: Pittheus makes Aegeus drunk and lets him lie with Aethra.

Polydectes.what: Polydectes tricks Perseus into promising the Gorgon's head.
Polydectes and his friends are turned to stone by Perseus.

Polyidus.what: Polyidus finds Glaucus and revives him with a herb learned from a serpent.
Polyidus teaches Glaucus divination, then makes him forget it by spitting.

Porphyrion.what: Porphyrion attacks Hera and is killed by the gods' assault.

Procles.what: Procles, twin son of Aristodemus, takes part in the lot-drawing for Lacedaemon.

Procne.what: Procne, wife of Tereus, avenges Philomela by killing Itys and serving him to Tereus; she becomes a nightingale.

Procris.what: Procris sleeps with Pteleon, flees to Minos, returns to Cephalus and is accidentally killed by him.

Pronous.what: Pronous, a son of Phegeus, is killed by Alcmaeon's sons.

Pyrrha.what: Pyrrha survives the flood with Deucalion in a chest and remakes people from stones.

Python.what: Python guards the oracle at Delphi and is killed by Apollo.

Rhoecus.what: Rhoecus, a centaur, is killed by Atalanta.

Salmoneus.what: Salmoneus impersonates Zeus and is punished by being struck down.

Semele.what: Semele, tricked by Hera, asks to see Zeus in his glory and is killed by his thunderbolt.

Side.what: Side, Orion's wife, is cast into Hades by Hera.

Sidero.what: Sidero is killed by Pelias and Neleus.

Sinis.what: Sinis kills travellers by bending pines and is killed by Theseus the same way.

Smyrna.what: Smyrna becomes the myrrh tree from which Adonis is born.

Sphinx.what: The Sphinx riddles the Thebans until Oedipus solves her riddle.

Syleus.what: Syleus is killed by Hercules while in Omphale's service.

Temenus.what: Temenus learns the oracle's true meaning and builds a fleet at Naupactus.
Temenus receives Argos in the lot-drawing and is later murdered by his sons.

Tereus.what: Tereus rapes and mutilates Philomela, is served his son Itys and becomes a hoopoe.

Thamyris.what: Thamyris challenges the Muses and is blinded by them.

The sons of Thestius.what: Thestius's sons take the boar's skin from Atalanta and are killed by Meleager.

Thyone.what: Thyone, Dionysus's mother, is brought by him from Hades up to heaven.

Tityus.what: Tityus assaults Latona and is shot by Apollo and Artemis, then punished in Hades.

Triptolemus.what: Triptolemus receives a dragon chariot and wheat from Demeter and sows it across the earth.

Tyro.what: Tyro bears twins Pelias and Neleus to Poseidon.

Zethus.what: Zethus with Amphion kills Lycus, binds Dirce to a bull, fortifies Thebes and expels Laius.

Eurypylus.what: Eurypylus, king of Cos, is killed when Hercules takes the island.

Fates.what: The Fates kill the giants Agrius and Thoas and trick Typhon into eating ephemeral fruits.
The Fates declare that Meleager will die when the brand burns.

Pandion.what: Pandion rules Athens; his daughters Procne and Philomela suffer at Tereus' hands.
Pandion is exiled to Megara while his sons retake Athens.

Perses.what: Perses, brother of Aeetes, is killed by Medea.

Zetes.what: Zetes, winged son of Boreas, sails with the Argonauts and helps free Phineus from the Harpies.
Zetes and Calais, sons of Boreas, are slandered by Idaea and later punish Phineus with the Argonauts.

Campe.what: Campe, jailoress of Tartarus, is slain by Zeus so he can free the Cyclopes.

Chione.what: Chione's son Eumolpus is cast into the sea; she is his mother in the Eleusis war story.

Delphyne.what: Delphyne, the half-beast she-dragon, guards Zeus's stolen sinews in the cave.

Dercynus.what: Dercynus, son of Poseidon, tries to rob Hercules and is killed.

Eteoclus.what: Eteoclus, one of the seven leaders, marches on Thebes and dies in the battle.

Gyes.what: Born a Hundred-hander to Sky and Earth, Gyes is bound by Sky in Tartarus.

Hestia.what: Hestia, firstborn of Cronus, is swallowed by her father to avoid the prophesied overthrow.

Hundred-handers.what: Freed by Zeus from Tartarus, the Hundred-handers help defeat the Titans and then guard them.

Mygdon.what: Mygdon, king of the Bebryces, is killed by Hercules in battle.

Phrasius.what: Phrasius, a Cypriot seer, is the first victim sacrificed in Egypt.

Podarces.what: Podarces is ransomed by Hesione and renamed Priam.

Poeas.what: Poeas lights Hercules' pyre on Oeta and receives his bow.

Polybotes.what: Polybotes is chased by Poseidon and crushed under Nisyrum.

Polygonus.what: Polygonus is killed in wrestling by Hercules at Torone.

Polyphemus.what: Polyphemus is left behind in Mysia and founds Cius.

Pteleon.what: Procris sleeps with Pteleon, then flees to Minos before returning to Cephalus

Tiphys.what: Tiphys, the Argo's helmsman, dies on the voyage
